subject: How long do you keep interaction records? (BrightBank)
messages:
From: Sara Thomas <sara.thomas@brightbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data retention: how long do you keep interaction records?

Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team is compiling a short list of retention questions for procurement before we move forward. Can you confirm the following for the hosted Redwood API (standard, non-dedicated account)?

1) Default retention windows: how long are request/response items (user prompts + model outputs) retained by default?
2) Streaming interim tokens / partial transcripts: are streamed tokens persisted anywhere after the session?
3) KV cache / session artifacts: any persistent stores?
4) Embeddings / indexable artifacts: default retention and deletion options?
5) Diagnostic and infrastructure logs: retention horizon and what you provide for audits (timestamps, operator IDs)?
6) How can a customer request deletion of specific interactions (single prompts) vs. bulk erasure? SLA for deletion and evidence?
7) Are attachments uploaded via the API stored and for how long? Are they scanned/parsed and stored as text?
8) Residency: will data for our account be stored in the US by default and can we force EU residency?

We attached our standard security questionnaire (BrightBank_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf) — you can answer the above at a high level; we may follow up with a call.

Appreciate a short written response we can share with procurement.

—Sara
Sara Thomas
Senior Information Security Manager, BrightBank
security@brightbank.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thomas <sara.thomas@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-07-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention: how long do you keep interaction records?

Hi Sara — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear list. I'll put together a concise written Q&A and loop in Legal to confirm wording for the procurement packet. High-level answers now so procurement can move forward:

• Request/response (prompts + final outputs): default capture window is 90 days for hosted (can be shortened for Dedicated/Private).
• Streaming/interim tokens: not persisted beyond the active session by default; we only retain finalized request/response artifacts unless the account enables transcript capture.
• KV cache/session artifacts: ephemeral and tied to the running instance; not stored as retrievable customer artifacts after the session ends.
• Embeddings/indexable outputs: default retention is 365 days; customers can opt for shorter horizons or set up automatic purge.
• Diagnostic/infrastructure logs: retention default 180 days; longer retention available as a paid add-on for audit evidence.

I'll follow up with a more detailed response including erasure runbook references and the support flow (how to raise an erasure request and what evidence we provide). Would you like a live call this week?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-07-20T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Draft answers for BrightBank retention Qs

Marcus — draft wording for the written Q&A. Please review and adjust tone as needed before sending to BrightBank. I'm intentionally concrete where possible.

"We retain finalized request/response records (user-submitted prompts and the model's final outputs) for 90 days by default for hosted accounts. This window is chosen to balance customer debugging needs and privacy. Customers using Dedicated or Private can configure retention to a shorter window (including immediate non-persistence) through account settings or by requesting a custom contract term.

Streaming tokens and intermediate partial transcripts are not written to persistent storage by default and are discarded once the session or stream ends. KV cache entries are in-memory and not exposed as retrievable artifacts after the session.

Embeddings and other indexable artifacts are stored by default for 365 days to support similarity search and downstream features; customers can request shorter retention or automated purging.

Diagnostic logs (request timestamps, route decisions, operator/event IDs) are retained 180 days by default; retention for audit purposes can be increased with an add-on.

Deletion/erasure: customers can request deletion of specific interactions or a bulk erase via the Redwood Support Portal or their account team. Deletion requests require the interaction identifier(s) and a confirmation step; targeted deletions are typically completed within 5 business days (bulk erasures may take longer depending on scope). We provide time-stamped deletion receipts and an audit trail for SOC2/assessment purposes.

Attachments uploaded via the API are stored encrypted at rest. We do not parse or persist attachment contents as plain text by default unless the customer explicitly requests text extraction; if extraction is used, derived text follows the same retention rules as prompts/outputs.

Residency: hosted accounts default to the customer's region (US for US accounts). We support EU residency for customers that opt into EU-hosted storage; this can be enforced in account configuration or via a Private deployment.

If you want, we can publish the above as a short one-page to include with procurement."

I recommend adding the erasure_runbook attachment for transparency.

—Marissa

Couple of legal edits and an operational note. Edited text below — feel free to pick the phrasing you prefer when responding externally. Also attaching our erasure runbook (erasure_runbook_v1.2.pdf) for the support flow.

Legal edits (short):
• Replace "immediate non-persistence" with "no-persistence option available for Dedicated/Private under contract".
• For deletions: clarify that deletion requests may require reasonable verification steps to prevent malicious erasure requests.

Operational note:
• Deletion SLA: targeted single-interaction deletes are policy to be completed within 5 business days; bulk account erases will be scoped with the customer and may take up to 30 days based on archival retention and backup cycles. We provide a signed deletion summary and an export of pre-deletion identifiers for customer records.

Kimberly

Subject: Re: Data retention: how long do you keep interaction records?

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise Q&A you can share with procurement; we've attached the erasure runbook and a short doc with regional residency options. If you'd like an annotated copy for your security team, we can join a call and walk through each item.

Q: How long do you keep user prompts and model outputs by default?
A: Hosted accounts: 90 days. Dedicated/Private: configurable by contract; can be shortened to meet regulatory needs, including a no-persistence option when requested in contract.

Q: Are streamed tokens persisted?
A: No. Streamed/interim tokens are discarded at the end of the session unless the account explicitly enables transcript capture.

Q: What about KV cache and session artifacts?
A: In-memory only; not retained as retrievable artifacts after the session terminates.

Q: Embeddings and indexable artifacts?
A: Default retention 365 days. Customers may request shorter retention or automated deletion workflows.

Q: Diagnostic/infrastructure logs?
A: Default 180 days. Extended retention available as an optional add-on for audit evidence.

Q: How can we request deletion?
A: Use the Redwood Support Portal (support.redwood.ai) or contact your account team. For targeted deletes provide interaction IDs; for bulk erasure we'll scope the request and provide a signed deletion summary and timeline. Targeted deletions: typically complete within 5 business days; bulk erases: up to 30 days depending on backups/archives.

Q: Attachments — are they stored as text?
A: Attachments are stored encrypted at rest. We do not extract or persist text from attachments unless the customer explicitly requests extraction; extracted text will follow the same retention policy as prompts/outputs.

Q: Data residency — where is our data stored?
A: Hosted accounts default to the customer region (US for US customers). Customers can opt into EU residency or choose a Private deployment to guarantee on-prem or regionally restricted storage.

Attachments: erasure_runbook_v1.2.pdf; BrightBank_retention_summary_2029.pdf (link included).

Would you like to schedule a 30-minute call to review with your security team?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales Engineering
